activity_context.topic_title: The Sum of the First N Terms of a Geometric Series

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given an Arbitrary Term and the Common Ratio
examples.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $3$rd term is $18$ and the common ratio is $3?$
examples.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine $a_1\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 18 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{(3-1)} \\ 18 & =9{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}	.
$$

In this case, $a_1=2$ and $r=3.$ Substituting our values into the formula for $S_N$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{2(1-{3}^{N})}{1-3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{2}(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & ={3}^{N}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $4+8+16+\,⋯?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=4$ and $r=2.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{4(1-{2}^{N})}{1-2} \\  & =-4(1-{2}^{N}) \\  & =4({2}^{N}-1).\end{aligned}
$$
